html:
Jawaharlal Nehru was a leader of India's independence movement and the first prime minister of India, from 1947 until his death in 1964. He held the office for almost 17 years, longer than anyone since.

He was the son of Motilal Nehru, a rich Allahabad lawyer and nationalist. He studied at Harrow and Cambridge and trained as a barrister in London. Back in India he joined the Indian National Congress and became the leader of its left wing. Gandhi backed him and named him his political heir. Nehru spent about nine years in British jails, where he wrote The Discovery of India and letters to his daughter, Indira.

He gave the "Tryst with Destiny" speech at midnight on 15 August 1947, the hour of Partition and independence. As prime minister he shaped the new state:

  • Parliamentary democracy and a secular state, written into the Constitution that Ambedkar steered.
  • Five-year plans with large state-owned industry, dams and steel works.
  • Science and higher education, starting with the first Indian Institute of Technology.
  • Nonalignment in the Cold War, a founding idea of the Non-Aligned Movement.

His record has dark spots. The dispute over Kashmir stayed unresolved, and China defeated India in the war of 1962, which hurt him badly. He died two years later. His daughter and grandson both became prime minister after him.
sum: Jawaharlal Nehru was a leader of India's independence movement and the first prime minister of India, from 1947 until his death in 1964. He held the office for almost 17 years, longer than anyone since.
